maria: Heads-up — saw repeated kernel-selection thrash on worker-7 during the long-chat workload. KV resident grew to ~36.2GB and we observed a ~30% p95 tail increase; one process hit OOM and restarted. Dumped a short profile below.

maria: ```
[2026-03-17T02:12:03Z] worker-7: model=redwood-compat-70B quant=8bit kernel_path=fast_path -> fallback
KV_SIZE_BYTES=38842060800
BATCH_TOKENS=512
ALLOC_FAIL: cudaMalloc at 0x7f.. (OOM)
Stack: runtime::batcher::admit -> kernel_selector -> cudaAlloc
```

sam: ugh. rough. is this on the int8 path or fallback float path? any kernel mismatch logs? :thinking:

maria: it's the quantized ABI but kernel_selector kept choosing the fused-attn kernel until mem pressure forced fallback to a less efficient kernel. attached a tiny trace snippet:

maria: ```
kernel_select_hist: fused_attn: 78%, fallback_attn: 22%
seq_len=2048 samples
heap_free_mb before: 5120
heap_free_mb after: 140
``` 

anya: hypothesis: our admission logic uses a static per-request token cap (512) and doesn't account for KV resident bytes. As KV grows, the headroom for activations shrinks and kernel paths change or OOM. Suggest dynamic token budget based on KV footprint.

anya: simple formula: \n`effective_token_budget = max(64, floor((gpu_free_mb - kv_reserved_mb) / per_token_kb) - safety_margin_tokens)`

anya: where `per_token_kb` is empirical (we use 1.8 KB/token for current kernels at seq<=2048), and `kv_reserved_mb` = ceil(kv_bytes/1e6) * kv_reservation_factor (default 1.1).

lina: also propose a soft-shedding knob: when kv_reserved_mb > kv_high_watermark reduce admission by 25% and set request.meta.prefetch=false so we avoid prefetching huge KV pages.

lina: config snippet:

lina: ```yaml
batch_admission:
  mode: dynamic
  base_per_token_kb: 1.8
  kv_reservation_factor: 1.1
  safety_margin_tokens: 48
  high_watermark_mb: 28000
  high_watermark_reduction_pct: 25
```

infra-bot: Experiment 'cache-orchestrate-2026-03-17' created by maria: canary=10% nodes=4 variant=dynamic-budget

sam: ran a 2h micro-benchmark with dynamic budget (per_token_kb=1.8, margin=48). p95 dropped from 620ms -> 420ms and we had zero cuda OOM restarts. throughput delta ~ -3% but tail & reliability way better.

sam: benchmark summary:

sam: ```
baseline: p95=620ms, restarts=3, avg_tokens_per_batch=490
dynamic: p95=420ms, restarts=0, avg_tokens_per_batch=312
```

maria: plan: roll the dynamic-budget canary to 10% traffic for 24h with metric guards: restarts==0 && p95 < 500ms. If green, expand to 50% and include kernel-selection heuristic bump.

anya: lgtm. I'll open a PR to update kernel-selector to prefer int8-dequantized path earlier under high KV pressure (heuristic: if kv_reserved_mb/gpu_total_mb > 0.4 -> bias weight to int8 kernels). Will add unit tests and a small sim harness.

lina: PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/infra/pull/1234 — added admission tests + a sim that fuzzes KV size vs seq len.

maria: thanks all. tagging @oncall to keep an eye on the canary overnight :eyes:

oncall: noted, I'll enable alert for any cuda OOMs and p95 regression > 100ms from baseline.

maria: one more note — let's capture kernel_select_hist and kv_size telemetry per-batch in the console so we can correlate before/after. small dashboard ticket incoming.

lina: opened dash ticket: https://console.redwood.ai/d/ops/cache-orchestrate-kv-telemetry

maria: ok closing thread for now, will post canary updates. :thumbsup:
